mainTopic: Whether one witness can disqualify a כהן, the sources for a חלל's and a בעל מום's service, and the משנה on a child's lineage
overview: The גמרא brings a proof that one witness is not believed in matters of forbidden relations. The proof is a ברייתא about a מקוה in יבנה that was assumed full but was measured and found too small. רבי טרפון says the earlier immersions are pure and רבי עקיבא says they are impure. Each compares the case to a כהן whose problem is found only after he served: a בן גרושה, whose service stays valid, or a בעל מום, whose service is invalid. רבי עקיבא shows that the מקוה is like the בעל מום, and רבי טרפון accepts this. The גמרא learns from the ברייתא that a silent בן גרושה still needs two witnesses, and אביי offers another way to read it: a blemish can simply be checked. Next the גמרא brings פסוקים showing why a חלל's past service counts and a בעל מום's does not. Then a new משנה gives four rules for whose status a child takes, and the גמרא begins questioning the first rule; the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Introducing a proof: the reservoir in Yavne
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the earlier claim and begins quoting a teaching from רבי שמעון about a reservoir in יבנה that was assumed full but measured short.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do I say this? From what we learned: רבי שמעון said, there was a story with the reservoir of Diskim in יבנה. Everyone assumed it was full, but they measured it and found it lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for the claim made just before, and it starts by telling the facts of a story. This step only sets up the case; the actual argument comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מנא אמינא לה' tells us a proof is coming for something already said: that one witness is not relied on for forbidden relations. The story itself is about a reservoir assumed to be a full מקוה that was later found short. The proof will come from a side remark in the debate about how many witnesses are needed (step 12).

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an opening that introduces a proof)
The assumed status of being complete (full enough for a מקוה)
Lacking or short of the needed amount

phrases.english: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: He wants a source for his earlier claim that one witness isn't believed about forbidden relations, like making a כהן into a חלל. The proof comes in step 12.

phrases.english: As we learned:
Rabbi Shimon said:
There was an incident with the reservoir of Diskim in Yavne
which stood with the presumption of being complete,
phrases.notes: 'Complete' means it held the full amount a מקוה needs, forty סאה.

phrases.english: and they measured it and it was found lacking.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the claim made just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier claim that one witness is not relied on in matters of forbidden relations and lineage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי שמעון about the reservoir of Diskim in יבנה

steps.title: The dispute: pure or impure?
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון rules that all the purifications done in the reservoir are pure, and רבי עקיבא rules that they are impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the purifications that were done in it, רבי טרפון declared pure and רבי עקיבא declared impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The two תנאים disagree about everyone and everything that was immersed in the reservoir before it was measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one knows when the water went down, so every past immersion is in doubt. רבי טרפון treats those immersions as valid, and רבי עקיבא treats them as not valid. Their reasons come in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Things (or people) made pure through immersion

phrases.english: All purifications that were done in it,
Rabbi Tarfon would declare pure,
and Rabbi Akiva would declare impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two rulings on the case just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון: the past immersions are pure. רבי עקיבא: they are impure.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: the מקוה keeps its status of being full
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון argues that the מקוה had a חזקה of being full, and a doubt should not take that status away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: This מקוה stands in its presumption of being full. You want to call it lacking because of a doubt. Do not call it lacking because of a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון explains his ruling by pointing to the מקוה's own חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the מקוה was once full, and we only know for sure that it was short at the moment it was measured. For all the time before that, we cannot be sure, and a doubt is not enough to remove a known status. So he treats the מקוה as full until it was measured.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:

phrases.aramaic: מִקְוֶה זֶה בְּחֶזְקַת שָׁלֵם הוּא עוֹמֵד,
phrases.english: This מקוה stands in the presumption of being whole;
out of doubt you come to make it lacking —
do not make it lacking out of doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְוֶה זֶה בְּחֶזְקַת שָׁלֵם הוּא עוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי טרפון's reason for ruling pure.
steps.raayaObject: רבי טרפון's ruling that the immersions are pure
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חזקה that the מקוה was full

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the person keeps his status of being impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers back with a different חזקה: the person who immersed was known to be impure, and a doubt should not make him pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: This person stands in his presumption of being impure. You want to make him pure because of a doubt. Do not make him pure because of a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back using the exact same reasoning style as רבי טרפון, but he points to the person's חזקה instead of the מקוה's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case now has two חזקות pulling in opposite directions. The מקוה was known to be full, but the person was known to be impure before he went in. רבי עקיבא says the person's impurity is what we hold onto, so a doubtful immersion does not change it.

keyTerms.meaning: The assumed status of being impure

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same rule, that you do not overturn a חזקה because of a doubt. They are not arguing about that rule. They are arguing about WHICH חזקה counts: the מקוה's or the person's.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם זֶה בְּחֶזְקַת טָמֵא הוּא עוֹמֵד,
phrases.english: This person stands in the presumption of being impure;
out of doubt you come to purify him —
do not purify him out of doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם זֶה בְּחֶזְקַת טָמֵא הוּא עוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טרפון's חזקה with an opposing חזקה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's reliance on the מקוה's חזקה of being full
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The person also has a חזקה, of being impure, and that חזקה points the other way.

steps.title: רבי טרפון's parable: the כהן who is a בן גרושה
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון compares the case to a כהן found to be a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה after serving, whose earlier service stays valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: This is like a כהן standing and offering on the מזבח, and then it becomes known that he is a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה. His service is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון brings a parable to back up his view: a problem found later does not cancel what was already done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this parable, a disqualification is discovered only after the כהן has already served, and the law is that his past service still counts. רבי טרפון says the מקוה is the same: finding out now that it is short does not cancel the immersions done in it before.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of a divorced woman (born to a כהן), who is disqualified from כהונה
The son of a woman who had חליצה (born to a כהן), also disqualified

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said: A parable —
to one standing and offering on the altar,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹדַע שֶׁהוּא בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ בֶּן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.english: and it became known that he is the son of a divorcee or the son of a חלוצה,
whose service is valid.
phrases.notes: This is the service he already did before anyone found out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: מָשָׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי טרפון supports his position with an analogy after רבי עקיבא's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: Past immersions stay valid even though the problem was found later
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law that a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה's earlier service is valid

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's parable: the כהן who is a בעל מום
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers with a different parable: a כהן found to be a בעל מום, whose service is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: This is like a כהן standing and offering on the מזבח, and then it becomes known that he has a blemish. His service is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא rejects רבי טרפון's comparison and offers a parable that leads to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too the problem is found only after the service, but this time the law is that the service is invalid. רבי עקיבא says the deficient מקוה is like this case, so the earlier immersions do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish, who may not serve

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: A parable —
to one standing and offering on the altar
and it became known that he is blemished,
whose service is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מָשָׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing analogy that reaches the opposite result from רבי טרפון's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי טרפון's choice of analogy, not the analogy method itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The deficient מקוה is better compared to a בעל מום, whose service is invalid, than to a בן גרושה.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: let's check which comparison fits
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון notes they each picked a different parable and proposes they work out which one the מקוה case really resembles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: You compared it to a בעל מום, and I compared it to a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. Let us see which it resembles. If it resembles a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, we will judge it that way. If it resembles a בעל מום, we will judge it like a בעל מום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון stops the back-and-forth and suggests a way to decide between the two parables. This step sets up the next move, where the actual comparison will be made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both parables involve a problem found after the service, yet they reach opposite results. So the real question becomes what makes them different, and which side the מקוה falls on. Whichever parable truly matches will decide the law for the מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see what it resembles

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that a doubt cannot overturn a חזקה. They disagree about which חזקה matters, and they turn the debate into a question of which parable fits: the בן גרושה, whose past service is valid, or the בעל מום, whose past service is invalid.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
You compared it to a blemished כהן,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי דִּמִּיתִיו לְבֶן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ לְבֶן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.english: and I compared it to the son of a divorcee or the son of a חלוצה;
let us see to which it is similar.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דּוֹמֶה לְבֶן גְּרוּשָׁה וּלְבֶן חֲלוּצָה –
phrases.english: If it is similar to the son of a divorcee or the son of a חלוצה,

phrases.aramaic: נְדוּנֶנּוּ כְּבֶן גְּרוּשָׁה אוֹ כְּבֶן חֲלוּצָה,
phrases.english: let us judge it like the son of a divorcee or the son of a חלוצה;
if it is similar to a blemished כהן,
let us judge it like a blemished כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה דִּימִּיתוֹ לְבַעַל מוּם, וַאֲנִי דִּמִּיתִיו לְבֶן גְּרוּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets out a method for deciding between the two competing parables.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which parable the deficient מקוה case truly resembles: the בן גרושה/בן חלוצה or the בעל מום

steps.title: First reason: one witness versus two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא argues that a מקוה and a בעל מום are both disqualified by one witness, unlike a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, who needs two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא began to reason: a מקוה can be disqualified by one witness, and a בעל מום can be disqualified by one witness. Do not try to prove otherwise from a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, because he can only be disqualified by two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers רבי טרפון's question from step 7 and shows which parable the מקוה case really matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares how much testimony each case needs. A מקוה and a בעל מום are each disqualified by one witness, so they belong together. A בן גרושה needs two witnesses, so רבי טרפון's parable does not fit the מקוה case.

keyTerms.meaning: through one person, meaning a single witness
through two people, meaning two witnesses

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva began to reason:
a ritual bath is disqualified through one person,
and a blemished priest is disqualified through one person,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה
phrases.english: and let the son of a divorcee or the son of a chalutza not prove otherwise,
since his disqualification is through two.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְחִיל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לָדוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טרפון's question of which parable the מקוה case resembles.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which parable fits the doubtful מקוה: a בן גרושה or a בעל מום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בעל מום, because both it and the מקוה are disqualified by a single witness.

steps.title: Second reason: a flaw in itself versus a flaw from others
steps.stepSummary: A second reason: a מקוה and a בעל מום are each flawed in themselves, while a בן גרושה is flawed because of other people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another reason: a מקוה is unfit because of something in the מקוה itself, and a בעל מום is unfit because of something in his own body. Do not try to prove otherwise from a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, because his problem comes from others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a second, separate reason why the מקוה matches the בעל מום and not the בן גרושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time he looks at where the problem comes from. A missing amount of water is a flaw in the מקוה itself, and a blemish is a flaw in the כהן's own body. The בן גרושה's body is fine; his problem comes from his parents' marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: in itself, in its own body
from others, coming from outside himself

phrases.english: Another explanation: a ritual bath's disqualification is in itself,
a blemished priest's disqualification is in himself,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה
phrases.english: and let the son of a divorcee or the son of a chalutza not prove otherwise,
since his disqualification comes from others.
phrases.notes: He means his mother: he is unfit only because of who she married.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent reason for the same answer given in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which parable fits the doubtful מקוה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בעל מום, because both it and the מקוה are flawed in themselves, unlike a בן גרושה.

steps.title: רבי טרפון accepts and praises רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון accepts רבי עקיבא's reasoning and praises him highly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said to him: עקיבא! Anyone who separates from you is like someone who separates from life itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון gives in and praises רבי עקיבא, which ends the debate and the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By praising רבי עקיבא, רבי טרפון shows that he accepts the comparison to a בעל מום. So the conclusion stands: a person who immersed in a מקוה later found to be lacking is treated as impure.

keyTerms.meaning: one who separates or turns away

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא ends with רבי עקיבא winning: the doubtful מקוה is like a בעל מום, and both are disqualified by one witness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said to him:
Akiva! Anyone who separates from you
is like one who separates from life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי טרפון accepts the reasoning of steps 8 and 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's view is accepted: the doubtful מקוה matches the בעל מום, so the person who immersed in it stays impure.

steps.title: What kind of בעל מום case is disqualified by one witness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means when it says one witness can disqualify a בעל מום, and concludes the כהן must have stayed silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: This blemished כהן who is disqualified by one witness, what is the case? If the כהן denies the claim, would one witness be believed? Rather, it must be a case where the כהן stays silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to its own discussion and starts examining the ברייתא's wording. This step sets up a proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן says the witness is wrong, one witness is not believed against him. So when the ברייתא says one witness disqualifies a בעל מום, it must be talking about a כהן who stays silent and does not deny it.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? what are the circumstances?

phrases.english: This blemished priest whose disqualification is through one witness,
what is the case?
If he denies it,
is the witness believed?
phrases.notes: This question expects the answer no: one witness is not believed against the כהן's denial.

phrases.english: Rather, it is where he is silent,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי בַּעַל מוּם שֶׁפְּסוּלוֹ בְּיָחִיד הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wording of רבי עקיבא's first reason in step 8 and asks what case it means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation does one witness disqualify a בעל מום?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only when the כהן stays silent and does not deny it.

steps.title: Proof: even a silent בן גרושה needs two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: Since the בעל מום case involves a silent כהן, the matching בן גרושה case must also involve a silent כהן. Yet the ברייתא says he needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same must be true of the בן גרושה or בן חלוצה: he is silent too. Yet the ברייתא teaches: a מקוה is disqualified by one witness and a בעל מום is disqualified by one witness, and do not try to prove otherwise from a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, who is disqualified only by two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. It shows from the ברייתא that one witness cannot disqualify a כהן as a בן גרושה, even when the כהן stays silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets the two cases side by side, so they must be talking about the same kind of situation, a silent כהן. For the בעל מום, one witness is enough. For the בן גרושה, the ברייתא still requires two witnesses, so silence does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: and in the same way, the matching case

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is repeating the ברייתא's words on purpose. Here they are a proof for the גמרא's own question, not a new argument by רבי עקיבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a rule: a single witness cannot make a כהן into a בן גרושה, even if the כהן does not deny it.

phrases.aramaic: וְדִכְוָתֵיהּ גַּבֵּי בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה
phrases.english: and similarly regarding the son of a divorcee or the son of a chalutza,
it is where he is silent,
and yet it teaches:
a ritual bath is disqualified through one witness
and a blemished priest is disqualified through one witness,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה
phrases.english: and let the son of a divorcee or the son of a chalutza not prove otherwise,
since his disqualification is through two.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִכְוָתֵיהּ גַּבֵּי בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה דְּשָׁתֵיק, וְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'silent' case from step 11 to the בן גרושה and draws the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That one witness cannot disqualify a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה even when he stays silent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's ברייתא, which pairs the בעל מום (one witness) with the בן גרושה (two witnesses) in the same silent situation.

steps.title: אביי: The כהן Denies It, But the Blemish Can Be Checked
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof from step 12. Both cases involve a כהן who denies the witness. The witness is still believed about a blemish because he can say 'undress and show us.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: really, the case is one where the כהן contradicts the witness. And to your question, 'why is the witness believed?', the answer is that he tells the כהן: take off your clothes and show us.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof from the silent כהן. He says the ברייתא is talking about a כהן who argues back, and the witness is believed only because the blemish can be checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed one witness can only be believed when the כהן stays silent. אביי says no: even if the כהן denies it, a blemish is on the body and anyone can look. The witness would not lie about something so easy to check, so he is believed. A בן גרושה claim cannot be checked this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (used to keep an earlier reading)
Undress and show (take off your clothes and let us see)

phrases.english: And אביי said:
Actually, it is a case where he contradicts him,
and as for what you said, 'Why is he believed?'
it is because he said to him: Undress and show.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם דְּקָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 12 by reading the case differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the בעל מום case must involve a silent כהן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof missed that a blemish can be checked, so a witness is believed even when the כהן denies it.

steps.title: The ברייתא's Wording Fits אביי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a מקוה and a בעל מום are flawed 'in themselves,' unlike a בן גרושה. This matches אביי: something in the object itself can be checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what the ברייתא teaches: a מקוה's flaw is in itself, and a בעל מום's flaw is in himself. Do not bring a proof from a בן גרושה or a בן חלוצה, whose flaw comes from others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא's own words support אביי's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Flawed in itself' now means more than a type of flaw. It means the flaw can be checked directly: measure the מקוה, look at the כהן's body. A בן גרושה's flaw depends on his mother's history, which cannot be seen on him, so it needs two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is taught (this fits the ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: A flaw in the thing itself can be checked, so one witness is enough. A flaw that comes from someone else's history cannot be checked, so it needs two witnesses.

phrases.english: And this is what is taught:
a ritual bath, its flaw is in itself,
and a blemished one, his flaw is in himself,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַל יוֹכִיחַ בֶּן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה
phrases.english: and do not let the son of a divorced woman or the son of a חלוצה prove otherwise,
since his flaw comes from others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up אביי's reading in step 13 with the ברייתא's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that a blemish is believed because it can be checked
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's contrast between 'פסולו בגופו' and 'פסולו מאחרים'

steps.title: Source That a Disqualified כהן's Service Counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the עבודה of a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the son of a divorced woman and the son of a חלוצה, whose service is valid: how do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants the source for the rule that this kind of כהן's past service still counts, and the next steps will give that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the סוגיא assumed that if a כהן turns out to be a בן גרושה, the עבודה he already did is not ruined. Now the גמרא asks which פסוק teaches this. This is surprising, since he is a חלל and should not serve at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of a woman who did חליצה (forbidden to a כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean he may serve to begin with. It only means the service he already did before he was found out is not thrown out.

phrases.english: And the son of a divorced woman and the son of a חלוצה,
whose service is valid, from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֶן גְּרוּשָׁה וּבֶן חֲלוּצָה דַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ כְּשֵׁירָה, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the witness debate to the source for a rule the ברייתא assumed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows a בן גרושה's past עבודה is valid.

steps.title: שמואל: "For Him and His Seed"
steps.stepSummary: שמואל learns it from the promise to פינחס: 'for him and his seed after him,' meaning both fit and unfit children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the פסוק says, 'And it shall be for him and his seed after him.' This includes both fit seed and unfit seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: the covenant of כהונה goes to all of פינחס's descendants, even the unfit ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His seed' is read broadly to include a חלל. Since the covenant of כהונה still covers him in some way, the service he already did counts.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
As the verse says:
"And it shall be for him and his seed after him"

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין זֶרַע כָּשֵׁר וּבֵין זֶרַע פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: both fit seed and unfit seed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about פינחס's 'seed' includes unfit children, so their service counts.

steps.title: שמואל's Father: "Bless His Substance"
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל learns it from 'Bless, ה׳, his substance (חילו), and accept the work of his hands.' He reads חילו as including his חולין, the unfit ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father said: from here, 'Bless, ה׳, his substance, and accept the work of his hands.' Even the profane ones in him, accept.
steps.whatsHappening: A second source for the same rule, from the blessing of the tribe of לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חילו sounds like חולין (profane). So the פסוק asks ה׳ to accept even the work of the 'profane' members of the tribe, meaning the חללים.

keyTerms.meaning: His substance or strength (read as hinting at חולין)
The profane ones among him (the חללים)

phrases.english: Shmuel's father said: from here:
"Bless, Lord, his substance,
and accept the work of his hands"
even the profane ones in him, You will accept.
phrases.notes: It's a wordplay: חֵילוֹ sounds like חוּלִּין, the unfit כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same rule as step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word חילו includes the חולין, so ה׳ accepts their service.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: "The כהן Who Will Be in Those Days"
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי learns it from 'the כהן who will be in those days.' Since nobody can go to a כהן of another time, the פסוק must mean a כהן who seemed fit then and was later found to be a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: from here, 'And you shall come to the כהן who will be in those days.' Could you think a person goes to a כהן who is not alive in his days? Rather, this is a כהן who was fit and then became a חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: A third source. It reads the extra words 'in those days' as teaching that a כהן's service counts for the time he was thought to be fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In those days' seems obvious, since of course you go to a living כהן. So the words must teach something new: go to whoever is the כהן now. If he is later found to be a חלל, what he did 'in those days' still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this cannot be the meaning)
Became (or was found to be) a חלל

steps.whatToRemember: Three sources (שמואל, אבוה דשמואל, רבי ינאי) all teach one rule: service already done by a כהן later found to be a חלל still counts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said: from here:
"And you shall come to the priest
who will be in those days."
But could it enter your mind
that a person goes to a priest
who was not in his days?
Rather, this is one who was fit and became a חלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third פסוק offered for the same rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'in those days' teach that a כהן later found to be a חלל was valid for his earlier service.

steps.title: Source for a blemished כהן's service being invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a בעל מום's עבודה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished כהן's service is invalid. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just found sources for why a בן גרושה's עבודה is valid. Now it asks the opposite question: where do we learn that a בעל מום's עבודה is invalid?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי עקיבא's parable assumed that a בעל מום's service is invalid even when the blemish is found only afterward. So far we have a source for the valid case. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק for the invalid case.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish

phrases.english: A blemished priest, whose service is invalid,
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעַל מוּם דַּעֲבוֹדָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question in Step 15, but for the invalid case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a בעל מום's עבודה is invalid

steps.title: שמואל: the covenant of peace belongs to a whole כהן
steps.stepSummary: שמואל learns it from 'בריתי שלום': the covenant applies when the כהן is whole, not when he is lacking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The פסוק says, 'Therefore say: Behold, I give him My covenant of peace (שלום).' This means when he is whole (שלם), and not when he is lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers with the פסוק about פינחס's covenant of כהונה. He reads the word 'שלום' as 'שלם', meaning 'whole'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The covenant of כהונה is tied to the כהן being complete in his body. A בעל מום is 'lacking', so he is outside that covenant, and his עבודה does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: My covenant of peace, given to פינחס

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
As the verse says:
"Therefore say: Behold, I give to him
My covenant of peace"
when he is whole
and not when he is lacking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שלום' is read as 'שלם': the covenant of כהונה applies only to a whole כהן

steps.title: But the word is spelled שלום, not שלם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק is written 'שלום', not 'שלם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'שלום'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's reading. The word in the פסוק is 'peace', so how can he read it as 'whole'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's derivation depends on reading the word differently. Its plain spelling, with a ו, means 'peace', so the challenge goes after the foundation of the proof.

phrases.english: But "shalom" (peace) is written!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״שָׁלוֹם״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading of שלום as שלם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The spelling of the word in the פסוק does not match the meaning 'whole'

steps.title: רב נחמן: the ו in שלום is broken
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the ו in שלום is written broken, so the word can be read as שלם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The ו of שלום is cut.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends שמואל. The ו in this word is written with a break in it, so it hints that the word can be read without the ו, as 'שלם'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The broken letter gives a textual basis for reading 'whole'. Because the ו is cut, the word can be read as 'שלם', and שמואל's reading stands: the covenant is given to a כהן who is whole.

keyTerms.meaning: A ו that is cut or broken

steps.whatToRemember: A בעל מום's עבודה is invalid because the covenant of כהונה ('בריתי שלום', read as 'שלם') belongs only to a כהן who is whole.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The vav of "shalom" is severed.
phrases.notes: In a ספר תורה, this ו is written with a break in it, so the word can be read as if the ו were missing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the written form of the letter supports the reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word is plainly 'שלום' with a full ו, so it cannot mean 'whole'
steps.terutzMaskana: The broken ו allows the word to be read as 'שלם'

steps.title: משנה rule 1: valid marriage with no sin, child follows the father
steps.stepSummary: Where there is קידושין and no עבירה, the child's status follows the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any case where there is קידושין and no עבירה, the child follows the male. Which case is this? A כהנת, a לויה, or a ישראלית who married a כהן, a לוי, or a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the first of four rules about whose status a child takes: in a permitted marriage, the child follows the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the קידושין takes effect and the marriage is fully permitted, the father decides the child's lineage. The example is any mix of כהן, לוי and ישראל families.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Follows the father' here means the child's family lineage (כהן, לוי or ישראל). It is not about being Jewish; that question is different.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Any case where there is betrothal
and there is no transgression,
the child follows the male.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזֶה זוֹ – זוֹ כֹּהֶנֶת, לְוִיָּה, וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִית
phrases.english: And which is this? This is a priest's daughter, a Levite's daughter, or an Israelite woman
who married a priest, a Levite, or an Israelite.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִידּוּשִׁין וְאֵין עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Valid קידושין with no עבירה: the child follows the father

steps.title: משנה rule 2: valid marriage with sin, child follows the flawed parent
steps.stepSummary: Where there is קידושין but also an עבירה, the child follows the flawed parent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any case where there is קידושין and there is an עבירה, the child follows the flawed parent. Which case is this? An אלמנה married to a כהן גדול; a גרושה or חלוצה married to a כהן הדיוט; a ממזרת or נתינה married to a ישראל; a בת ישראל married to a ממזר or a נתין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its second rule. The marriage takes effect but is forbidden, so the child takes the status of whichever parent is flawed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קידושין still works, but because of the עבירה the child does not simply follow the father. He takes the lower status. For example, a כהן's son from a גרושה is a חלל, and a ממזרת's child with a ישראל is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary כהן (not the כהן גדול)
A woman descended from the גבעונים
A woman released from יבום through חליצה

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִידּוּשִׁין וְיֵשׁ עֲבֵירָה –
phrases.english: And any case where there is betrothal and there is a transgression,
the child follows the flawed one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזֶה זוֹ – זוֹ אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: And which is this? This is a widow married to a High Priest,
a divorcée or a chalutza married to an ordinary priest,
a mamzeret or a Gibeonite woman married to an Israelite,
an Israelite woman married to a mamzer or a Gibeonite.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִידּוּשִׁין וְיֵשׁ עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second rule of the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Valid קידושין with an עבירה: the child follows the flawed parent

steps.title: משנה rule 3: no קידושין with him but yes with others, child is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: If her קידושין cannot take effect with this man but can with other men, the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone whose קידושין cannot take effect with him, but can take effect with others, the child is a ממזר. Which case is this? One who has relations with any of the עריות in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third rule. In a relationship with one of the עריות, קידושין cannot take effect at all, and the child is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether קידושין could take effect between these two people. She is Jewish and could marry other men, but not this one, because they are an ערוה to each other. That is what creates ממזרות.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden union where קידושין cannot take effect
The forbidden relationships listed in the תורה

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עָלָיו קִידּוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: And anyone who cannot have betrothal with him,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָהּ עַל אֲחֵרִים קִידּוּשִׁין –
phrases.english: but can have betrothal with others,
the child is a mamzer.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזֶה זֶה – זֶה הַבָּא עַל אַחַת
phrases.english: And which is this? This is one who has relations with one
of all the forbidden relations in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עָלָיו קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third rule of the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When קידושין cannot take effect between them because of an ערוה, the child is a ממזר

steps.title: משנה rule 4: no קידושין with anyone, child is like the mother
steps.stepSummary: If her קידושין cannot take effect with any Jew, the child has the mother's status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone whose קידושין cannot take effect with him or with others, the child is like her. Which case is this? The child of a שפחה or a נכרית.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its fourth and last rule. If the mother cannot marry any Jew at all, the child simply takes her status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שפחה or a נכרית cannot have קידושין with any Jew, so the father does not count for the child's status. The child is a slave or a non-Jew like her, not a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The child is like the mother

steps.whatToRemember: Four levels: (1) קידושין and no עבירה: the child follows the father; (2) קידושין with an עבירה: the child follows the flawed parent; (3) no קידושין with him but yes with others: the child is a ממזר; (4) no קידושין with anyone: the child is like the mother.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ לֹא עָלָיו
phrases.english: And anyone who cannot have betrothal neither with him
nor with others,
the child is like her.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזֶה זֶה – זֶה וְלַד שִׁפְחָה וְנׇכְרִית.
phrases.english: And which is this? This is the child of a maidservant or a gentile woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ לֹא עָלָיו וְלֹא עַל אֲחֵרִים קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth and final rule of the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When she cannot have קידושין with any Jew, the child takes the mother's status

steps.title: Is the father rule really true in every case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's first rule. רבי שמעון asks רבי יוחנן whether it is truly a fixed rule that wherever there is קידושין and no עבירה, the child follows the father. He begins to bring a case that seems to go against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: "Any case where there is קידושין..." רבי שמעון said to רבי יוחנן: Is it really a fixed rule that whenever there is קידושין and no transgression, the child follows the father? But there is...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting the first line of the משנה. Then רבי שמעון starts to challenge it, and this line sets up a counter-example that comes right after "הרי".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated its rule in very broad terms: "כל מקום", any case at all. רבי שמעון asks whether the word "כל" can really be true. Saying "הרי" tells us he has a real case in mind where there is קידושין and no עבירה, but the child does not follow the father.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
A fixed, general rule that always applies
The child follows the father's status
A transgression, meaning a forbidden marriage
"But there is...", which introduces a counter-example

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends in the middle of the question. "הרי" is not the end of the thought. The case that seems to break the rule is brought right after this.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"Any case where there is betrothal"
phrases.notes: This quotes the first rule of the משנה, from step 23.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Is it a fixed rule

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִידּוּשִׁין וְאֵין עֲבֵירָה
phrases.english: that any case where there is betrothal and there is no transgression,
the child follows the male?
But there is...

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָלָא הוּא דְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ קִידּוּשִׁין וְאֵין עֲבֵירָה הַוָּלָד הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַזָּכָר הֲרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה, aiming at the first rule (step 23).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's broad rule that wherever there is קידושין and no עבירה, the child follows the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "כל" ("any") claims the rule has no exceptions. רבי שמעון is about to bring a case with valid קידושין and no עבירה where the child does not follow the father.
